Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu says rising memory and AI token prices are making business very difficult: ‘We have …’
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu: Memory prices have made business ‘very difficult’

Sridhar Vembu says the era of ‘free’ memory is over

Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu has raised concerns over the sharp rise in computer memory prices, saying the increase, along with the cost of AI tokens, is making it harder to run businesses. Sridhar Vembu was responding to a Tom’s Hardware report that said memory prices have jumped as much as 500% in the past 12 months, with some DDR5 RAM kits now costing nearly 10 times their lowest recorded prices. The Zoho founder said companies have so far tried to avoid passing these higher costs to customers, but added that holding prices steady is becoming increasingly difficult.Reacting to the report in a post on X, Sridhar Vembu wrote: “Memory prices, along with AI token prices have made business very difficult. We have held back from raising prices but it is becoming hard.”His comments come as memory prices have climbed sharply over the past year. According to historical pricing data cited by Tom's Hardware, a 64GB DDR5-5600 kit that averaged around $191 in August 2025 was priced at about $1,118 in August 2026, an increase of about 485%.Higher-capacity memory has seen an even bigger jump from its previous lows. A 128GB DDR5-6400 kit was recently listed at $3,399, compared with a lowest tracked price of $329.The increase is not limited to DDR5. DDR4 prices have also risen, with the report showing year-on-year increases ranging from about 120% to 177% across the memory kits it tracked.In the post, Sridhar Vembu also used the sharp price increase to make a broader point about how software is developed. He argued that programming languages and software tools will have to become more efficient as memory becomes more expensive.“A techncial note: for a long time, programming languages were designed with the assumption that memory is ‘free’. That era has now ended. We need highly memory efficient languages and smarter compilers, even for AI to use,” Vembu wrote.He added: “Safety of code and productivity in writing code cannot come at the expense of memory bloat. That is my area of research.”
Article Summary: Sridhar Vembu: Memory prices have made business ‘very difficult’ He was responding to a Tom’s Hardware report that said memory prices have jumped as much as 500% in the past 12 months. Zoho founder said companies have so far tried to avoid passing these higher costs to customers, but added that holding prices steady is becoming increasingly difficult.

Article Title: Apple left a video of its camera AirPods inside a Mac update, and this is what they look like
Article Text:
Apple demoed a camera you can't see, in a video it didn't mean to publish.

AirPods cameras are for Siri, not for you to click photos

A frame from the demo video Apple left in macOS 26.7, alongside a closer look at the bud. The stem is thicker than the AirPods Pro 3. (Image: MacRumors/Aaron Perris)

Apple employees have been wearing prototypes for months

A September launch could be on the table, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro

The first real look at Apple's camera AirPods didn't come from the usual suspects. It came from Apple, by mistake. Buried in the macOS Tahoe 26.7 release candidate that landed Monday is a short demo video showing a man wearing AirPods holding up a book, with a Siri voiceover explaining that Visual Intelligence makes "your world becomes savable" and that you can ask it to save what you're looking at for later. MacRumors found the clip.You have to look twice to spot what's different. The bud in the video could pass for an AirPods Pro 3. No visible lens, no sensor housing, just a stem that reads slightly thicker than the current one. MacRumors also found the release candidate littered with references to codename B790, including an error string about an image stream failing on the left bud. Elsewhere in the same build: a warning telling users to keep the AirPods uncovered so the system can read their surroundings accurately. Long hair, evidently, is a known problem.What the cameras actually do is narrower than it sounds. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, they capture low-resolution visual information for Siri to reason about, not photos or video. Look at what's in your fridge, ask what to cook. Walk somewhere and get directions that account for what's in front of you.The demo fits that description. Nobody takes a picture in it. A man looks at a book, Siri saves the book, and that is the whole feature.Gurman has also described longer stems and an LED that lights up when visual data goes to the cloud. Neither turns up in the video.Apple testers have been using prototypes daily since at least May, Bloomberg reported at the time, at the design validation test stage. That is the step immediately before production validation, which means the physical design is locked and what follows is a manufacturing problem rather than a product one. Everything after DVT is about yields and tooling. It also explains why the software looks finished. A team that far along has hardware stable enough to build onboarding screens against, which is exactly what turned up in macOS this week.Earlier this month, Bloomberg reported that camera AirPods could arrive as soon as this year, pulling forward a device most people had penciled in for 2027. Apple's iPhone event is expected in early September, where the iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max and the first foldable iPhone are due.One wrinkle worth keeping straight: B790 is not the camera AirPods Gurman has been writing about since 2025. That model, B798, slipped to 2027 after Apple's Siri delays. B790 is a separate project that got there first.Apple, as usual, hasn't confirmed any of it. But a release candidate is the last build before public release, and this one already has setup screens and error messages for the thing. That normally means the hardware is done. September will tell us the rest.
Article Summary: AirPods cameras are for Siri, not for you to click photos. The bud in the video could pass for an AirPods Pro 3. Apple employees have been wearing prototypes for months. A September launch could be on the table, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro.

Article Title: Why Google is making headlines in Berkshire's biggest quarter of stock-buying following Warren Buffett's exit as CEO
Article Text:
Warren Buffett ’s legacy and Abel’s role

Other portfolio changes

Cash deployment

Berkshire Hathway has sharply increased its stake in Alphabet during its biggest quarter of stock buying in years. According to a report by Business Insider, under CEO Greg Abel, Berkshire boosted its holdings by 83% to about 106 million shares worth $38 billion at the end of June in Alphabet. The conglomerate agreed to purchase $10 billion worth of Alphabet stock at a discount in a private placement in June, and added another 19.6 million shares on the open market last quarter. Alphabet is now Berkshire’s third‑largest US holding, behind Apple ($66 billion) and American Express ($51 billion).The size of the Alphabet bet stands out given Buffett's long-standing reluctance to invest heavily in technology stocks throughout most of his career, with Apple as the notable exception. He has historically preferred businesses like Coca-Cola and Geico over tech names. Even so, Buffett has said he personally made the call to invest in Alphabet last year, and with Abel now serving as CEO while Buffett remains chairman, the position appears to reflect shared decision-making between the two rather than a clean break from Buffett's past preferences.Alphabet's stock has climbed roughly 170% over the past three years, with investors continuing to bet that the search-and-advertising giant will emerge as one of the biggest beneficiaries of the ongoing AI boom.Alphabet wasn't the only shift in Berkshire's holdings last quarter. The firm boosted its stake in Delta Air Lines by 44%, bringing that position to $5.4 billion as of June 30. It also established a new stake in D.R. Horton and added significantly to its existing positions in Lennar and Macy's.On the other side of the ledger, Berkshire roughly halved its stakes in Capital One and Nucor, trimmed its holdings in Bank of America and Kroger, and exited a smaller position in Constellation Brands entirely.The second‑quarter update showed Berkshire spent $23.5 billion on stocks while selling only $3.7 billion, ending 14 straight quarters as a net seller. It also executed $4.5 billion in buybacks, reducing its cash pile from $380 billion to $365 billion.
Article Summary: Alphabet is now Berkshire’s third‑largest US holding, behind Apple ($66 billion) and American Express ($51 billion) The firm also boosted its stake in Delta Air Lines by 44%, bringing that position to $5.4 billion as of June 30.

Article Title: Biggest US grid operator has a ‘shutdown proposal’ that shows tension between data centers and power grids in America
Article Text:
Representative image

Why grid operators are worried with rapid expansion of datacenters

PJM Interconnection, the largest electrical grid operator in the US, has proposed a framework that would require data centers to switch to backup generators when regional power reserves hit dangerously low levels. According to a report in Reuters, the proposal aligns with President Donald Trump's "Ratepayer Protection Pledge," a non-binding initiative aimed at shielding residential consumers from escalating costs tied to surging data center power demands, according to PJM.Under the proposed emergency procedure, utilities would be instructed to curtail or transfer electricity demand from data centers and other heavy energy consumers before imposing blackouts on residential households. This means that PJM Interconnection is proposing a shutdown of data centers in emergencies. In the event that the power grid is in danger of shutting down, they want data centers to be shut down first.However, PJM noted that it currently lacks direct authority to mandate such curtailments and must rely on cooperation from individual state regulators.PJM manages electricity distribution for 67 million people across a 13-state region stretching from Washington, D.C.to Chicago. The move underscores intensifying friction between the rapid expansion of energy-hungry data infrastructure and the capacity of the aging U.S. power grid.The grid operator's recent capacity auction saw prices hit a regulatory cap of $325 per megawatt-day. Despite those price signals designed to spur new power generation, PJM still faced a roughly 6.8-gigawatt shortfall against its projected reliability requirements, heightening the risk of system-wide blackouts.To better manage system loads, PJM is also seeking to establish a registry to monitor the locations and power consumption of data centers and other massive electricity users. The rapid proliferation of data facilities has evolved into a contentious political issue across PJM's footprint, notably in Northern Virginia, which hosts the world's largest concentration of data hubs. Local communities increasingly voice concerns over noise, neighborhood disruption, and the risk of absorbing the utility bills required to power the tech sector's expansion.
Article Summary: PJM Interconnection, the largest electrical grid operator in the US, has proposed a framework that would require data centers to switch to backup generators when regional power reserves hit dangerously low levels. The move underscores intensifying friction between the rapid expansion of energy-hungry data infrastructure and the capacity of the aging power grid.

Article Title: In 2005 for the first time, scientists documented giant squid in their natural habitat, since then many mysteries about their lives remain in ...
Article Text:
A diorama unlike any other in the museum

The real-life battle behind the display

Decades of mystery, only recently interrupted

An unassuming black box near the American Museum of Natural History's iconic blue whale draws in unsuspecting visitors to one of the museum's most striking exhibits, according to a Popular Science report. Every few seconds, a light flashes inside an otherwise pitch-black display, briefly revealing a row of sharp teeth and reddish tentacles as a sperm whale clamps down on a giant squid. The Sperm Whale and Giant Squid Diorama offers a rare, dramatic glimpse into one of the ocean's most mysterious predator-prey relationships, one that scientists are still working to fully understand.Unlike most of AMNH's other displays, this diorama has no glass front. Instead, its dark, reflective interior creates a mirror-like effect that reportedly confused early visitors into thinking the exhibit was empty. The darkness isn't incidental, it's designed to recreate the lightless conditions of the deep ocean, where sunlight never reaches.That same design also makes the diorama unusually labor-intensive to clean. In a video recently shared on social media, AMNH Exhibition Maintenance staffer Janet Spiller can be seen using a backpack vacuum fitted with fiber pole attachments to reach into the exhibit's nooks and crannies, a job that can take a single person up to four hours to complete.The scene depicted in the diorama reflects a genuine and extreme biological encounter. Sperm whales (Physeter macrocephalus) are known to dive more than 6,500 feet, a depth equivalent to stacking roughly four and a half Empire State Buildings on top of one another, and can remain submerged for over 60 minutes at a time in pursuit of giant squid (Architeuthis dux).Much of what scientists know about this underwater clash comes from indirect evidence rather than direct observation. Sperm whales are sometimes found with circular marks on their skin, believed to be sucker marks left behind from squid fighting to escape. Researchers have also recovered giant squid beaks, the hard biting structures used by the animal, inside the stomachs of sperm whales, offering further proof of these deep-sea encounters.Despite the drama depicted in exhibits like this one, giant squid remain one of the ocean's most elusive animals. Scientists did not document a giant squid in its natural habitat on camera until 2005, and even now, many aspects of the species' life in the deep ocean remain largely unknown. The persistence of that mystery is part of what continues to make the predator-prey relationship between sperm whales and giant squid such a compelling subject for both researchers and museum visitors alike.
Article Summary: The Sperm Whale and Giant Squid Diorama offers a rare, dramatic glimpse into one of the ocean's most mysterious predator-prey relationships. Unlike most of AMNH's other displays, this diorama has no glass front. Its dark, reflective interior creates a mirror-like effect that reportedly confused early visitors into thinking the exhibit was empty.

Article Title: How Silverfox cybercriminal group is using Claude to target companies in India and other Asian countries
Article Text:
Representative Image

“SilverFox is one of the most active threat groups in the whole APAC region. They get into targets through three simple routes: fake websites, phishing emails, and harmful files spread via social messaging apps. They inject malware used for long-term cyberespionage and sensitive data gathering. Our recent analysis showed they are now distributing fake Claude for Windows, macOS, and Linux, leveraging AI use in companies to crack into their targets’ security defenses,”

How SilverFox uses fake Claude apps to target companies

SilverFox attacks remain concentrated in Asia

AI is changing the speed and scale of cyberattacks

“In this particular case, disclosed by our Sysdig, the malicious AI agent completed the entire cycle of diagnosing a failed attempt, correcting its approach, and launching a new attack in just 31 seconds, far outpacing the response capabilities of most human defenders. Beyond speed, JADEPUFFER also demonstrates an unprecedented level of autonomy. It shows that AI agents are now capable of making independent decisions throughout the attack process, effectively replicating the reasoning of an experienced human attacker without direct oversight,”

How companies can defend against AI-powered attacks

SilverFox, an Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) group, is using fake Claude apps to target companies in India and other countries in the Asia Pacific region. According to researchers from Kaspersky’s Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT), the cybercriminal group is exploiting the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in businesses to distribute malware and gain access to target networks.explains Ye Jin (Seth), Lead Security Researcher at Kaspersky GReAT.Kaspersky researchers said SilverFox has used a multi-stage attack process and segmented infrastructure, with different addresses and domains used at different stages. The approach can make it harder for security teams to identify and block the complete attack chain.The group’s recent campaign targeted organisations in India, Indonesia, South Africa and Russia across industrial, consulting, trade and transportation sectors. Attackers sent phishing emails designed to appear like official tax audit notifications or messages asking recipients to download an archive containing a supposedMore than 1,600 malicious emails were detected in January-February 2026, according to Kaspersky data. The emails often used a sense of authority and urgency, similar to messages about taxes, to trick people into opening malicious files and launching the attacks.More recent findings indicate that SilverFox has expanded its tactics to fake versions of Claude for Windows, macOS and Linux. Claude is an AI assistant developed by Anthropic that can be used for writing, coding, analysing documents and other tasks.Kaspersky said the APAC region accounts for the largest share of SilverFox’s malicious activity, with attack volumes exceeding those recorded across other regions combined.“Based on our current threat data, Greater China is SilverFox’s main target, with over 90% of all its attacks targeting the region. Mainland China alone makes up 71%. Myanmar, Cambodia and Singapore also see lots of attacks. These are the next hotspots we need to watch,” adds Ye Jin.Manufacturing accounts for more than one-third of the group’s attacks, making it the most targeted industry in Kaspersky’s current data. IT and services are also frequently targeted, while healthcare and finance remain among the sectors facing attacks from the group.Kaspersky’s Ye Jin also highlighted the emergence of AI-driven attacks that can automate decisions and parts of the attack process. One example is JADEPUFFER, described as an LLM-driven ransomware attack that demonstrated how an AI agent could analyse a failed attempt, change its approach and launch another attack.he explains.Another example highlighted by the researcher is ChatGPhish, an indirect prompt injection technique in which malicious instructions are hidden inside webpages. When a user asks an AI assistant to summarise such a page, the embedded instructions can potentially be processed by the AI and surfaced as part of its response.Kaspersky also pointed to VoidLink, an AI-assisted cloud-native malware framework reported in January 2026, as an example of how generative AI can reduce the technical effort required to develop malware.Kaspersky recommends that organisations adapt their security measures as attackers increasingly use AI and automated techniques. Its suggested measures include proactive AI-driven threat hunting to identify unknown threats, alongside Zero Trust architecture that verifies access requests rather than automatically trusting users or devices inside a network.The company also recommends a systematic defence covering endpoints, networks, applications and data. Another approach is using AI models and other dual-use AI technologies to improve threat detection and response and adapt security measures as attack techniques change.The growing use of AI by both attackers and defenders means organisations need to account for AI-assisted phishing, malware distribution and automated attack processes alongside conventional cybersecurity threats.
Article Summary: SilverFox, an Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) group, is using fake Claude apps to target companies in India and other countries in the Asia Pacific region. The group’s recent campaign targeted organisations in India, Indonesia, South Africa and Russia across industrial, consulting, trade and transportation sectors.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos: “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of…”
Article Text:
Image: AP News

Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos

“I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.”

What does this quote mean?

Limitations can force us to think differently

Necessity has a long history of creating innovation

Frugality can make innovation more efficient

Constraints can turn problems into creative challenges

Creativity often grows outside the comfort zone

Why this quote still matters today

Innovation is often associated with having more, more money, more resources, more advanced technology and more time. But some of the most creative solutions emerge when those advantages are limited. Jeff Bezos captured this idea when he said, “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.” His words suggest that limitations do not always prevent progress. Sometimes, they force people to think differently, question familiar methods and find solutions that would never have emerged in more comfortable circumstances.Jeff Bezos (1964-present) is an American entrepreneur and founder of Amazon. He built the company from an online bookseller into one of the world's largest technology and e-commerce businesses and has also pursued ventures in space exploration through Blue Origin. His observation highlights how constraints can turn necessity into a catalyst for experimentation and inventive thinking.This statement implies that scarcity of resources can be an impetus for innovation. When there are no simple solutions, people are obliged to rethink how to do things. Tight budget, shortage of materials, or technical difficulties can become the grounds for experimenting rather than excuses for inaction. The main message that Bezos tries to convey here is that constraints can make people innovative.In the case of abundance of resources, it is easy to find a solution by adding more resources, people, tools or funds. Constraints take away that luxury. All of a sudden, efficiency becomes the priority, and common assumptions should be questioned. A constrained team might discover a simpler way of doing things just because they do not have enough means to operate according to the traditional way.Useful innovations have often been developed due to people’s needs for solving certain problems using what was already available at hand. In cases ranging from simple farming implements to sophisticated medical gadgets that operate in conditions of limited resources, necessity has proved time and again to breed creativity. In the absence of an apparent solution, people start to search for other ways of solving their problems.Innovation does not necessarily mean that you should develop something that is larger or more complicated than your current product. Some of the most outstanding solutions come when people try to do the same thing using less material resources or reducing superfluous steps in a process. This way, frugality may become another incentive for inventors to find what really matters.It may seem as if a hard constraint makes the issue a roadblock. However, perceiving a limitation as a challenge will make a difference in the mindset when it comes to dealing with an issue. The question from “Why can't we do this?” will turn into “How could we do this differently?” This approach can foster experimenting and coming up with unique ideas.Comfort can help one to carry on with the things as usual. Constraints break up the sense of comfort. They make one think and come up with new options. Regardless of whether one is starting a business, developing a product or even solving a simple problem, constraints can provide a different perspective of creativity than abundance can.Whether it be startups trying to innovate on meager resources or scientists innovating the technology to suit a harsh environment, innovations often emerge when there is a sense of urgency involved. The words of Jeff Bezos provide an excellent point that lack of resources should not necessarily translate into lack of opportunities. In some cases, the very fact that there is no easy way out leads to innovation of a solution. The lesson from the statement is quite straightforward: Innovation occurs when nothing else works.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos is an American entrepreneur and founder of Amazon. He said, “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out” His words suggest that limitations do not always prevent progress.

Article Title: Nick Long, Mayor of League City in Texas, joins H-1B visa debate; says: H-1B program should not be used by any ...
Article Text:
The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position

Public universities are H-1B cap-exempt

Nick Long, Mayor of League City in Texas has joined the H-1b visa debate publicly. Long recently said in an X post that no public organisation should use the H-1B program, arguing taxpayer-funded jobs should go to taxpayers in response to Texas State University's filing for a Public Relations Specialist role. Nick Long’s comments came in response to a post announcing that the Texas State University (@txst) has filed a notice of intent to hire an H-1B Public Relations administrator.The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position. The filing prompted Scott Bowen, Republican nominee for Texas House of Representatives, to share the post on his timeline writing: “Texas State graduates hundreds of communication majors every year. Not one of them was qualified for this job?”.Nick Long quoted the post and wrote: “No public entity should be using H-1B program. Taxpayers should get taxpayer funded jobs”.Under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA § 214(g)(5)(A) and (B)), certain categories of H1B petitions are exempt from the annual numerical cap of 65,000 (plus 20,000 master's cap). This means they can sponsor eligible foreign workers for H-1B visas throughout the year without participating in the annual lottery.The exemption also applies to nonprofit entities affiliated with higher education institutions and certain nonprofit or government research organisations.In other news, a new research indicates a projected decline in international student enrollment for Fall 2026. Preliminary analysis by NAFSA: Association of International Educators and JB International shows cascading effects on US economic contribution and jobs supported. This downturn reflects the convergence of several headwinds: declining application volumes, persistent visa appointment bottlenecks, and newly restrictive immigration policy changes.
Article Summary: The debate began after Texas State University filed a notice of intent to sponsor an H-1B visa for a Public Relations Specialist position. Nick Long quoted the post and wrote: “No public entity should be using H- 1B program. Taxpayers should get taxpayer funded jobs’

Article Title: Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings on why he stopped calling CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters about the business: They can mimic me and...
Article Text:
Reed Hastings on leaving the Netflix board: 'like being a godparent versus a parent'

The Warner Bros. Discovery call Netflix made without its founder in the room

Netflix's co-founder Reed Hastings spent 29 years at Netflix and now sends its two CEOs almost nothing. Not because anything soured — the opposite. He says Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters have absorbed his thinking so completely that phoning them is redundant. He's tested that theory in the biggest way possible. When Netflix walked away from the Warner Bros. Discovery deal this year, its founder wasn't in the room for the call.Speaking on Semafor's The CEO Signal podcast, hosted by Penny Pritzker and Andrew Edgecliffe-Johnson, the Netflix co-founder said he's been "very disciplined" about not calling the co-CEOs on business matters since leaving the board in June. He tried, briefly. For the first couple of months he lobbed in the occasional thought, then noticed something: they could already run the simulation without him. They ask what Reed would think, set that answer aside, and do what they believe is right. Which, Hastings said, is what they should do. "They can mimic me and conjure me easily. I'm very predictable in that way."The social side hasn't gone anywhere—he still talks to them and they hang out.What changed was the front line. Hastings stepped down as Netflix CEO in January 2023 and left the board this June, and he's blunt that the second exit was the smaller one. Being on a board of a company doing well, he said, is a fairly relaxed gig. The genuinely disorienting part was the workload dropping from around 70 hours a week to roughly one.The clearest proof of the handover came this year, when Netflix walked away from the Warner Bros. Discovery deal. Hastings says he wasn't involved in that decision at all. Sarandos and Peters worked the trade-offs themselves. He describes it as a price question rather than a strategy one—Netflix was comfortable with what it had offered, Larry Ellison raised the bid, Netflix had the chance to match and chose not to.Hastings frames the whole shift as moving from parent to godparent. The company, he added, has to stop reliving how he did things and start making its own mistakes.
Article Summary: Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings left the board in June. He says he's been "very disciplined" about not calling the co-CEOs on business matters. Hastings frames the whole shift as moving from parent to godparent. The company, he added, has to stop reliving how he did things.

Article Title: Few years ago, US store owner found 97 ultra rare vintage Mario game cartridges: They are now up for auction
Article Text:
A casual scrap-metal purchase turns into a ‘Holy Grail’

Cassettes get record-breaking grades from authenticators

Auction details and charity announcement

A box of 97 factory-fresh vintage Nintendo video games that sat untouched in a US storage for years has officially hit the auction block, putting one of the most unusual discoveries in retro gaming history up for public bidding on Friday (August 14). According to a report, this collection consists of 97 uncirculated copies of the classic Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt combination cartridge. Originally released for the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) in 1988, these specific copies carry a 1993 manufacturing date – two years after the title was thought to be discontinued, essentially making them the last known production run and a previously undocumented variant in gaming archives. The online sale began through Goldin's Pop Culture Auction and will run through September 9.The discovery was made when Kevin Braun, owner of One Stop Wonders in Waukesha, Wisconsin, asked long-time Nintendo collector and Nintendo Wire founder Jason Ganos to help appraise and sell common games and Pokémon cards. During the conversation, Braun brought up a forgotten box of cartridges he had previously bought from a customer whose family originally saved them for scrap metal.When Ganos examined the games, he discovered that all 97 copies were in flawless, unplayed condition. As Nintendo officially ended standard production of the combination bundle in 1991, collectors believe this unexpected 1993 batch was produced either as warranty replacement inventory or for a retail store promotion that never made it to shelves.Realising the potential value of the uncirculated batch, Ganos personally transported all 97 game cartridges in his carry-on luggage to California for professional authentication and grading. Examiners at Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) graded the entire batch, awarding five of the 97 cartridges a flawless “Gem Mint 10.” According to Ganos, PSA had never previously awarded a perfect 10 grade to an original NES cartridge.While high-grade vintage video games have commanded six-figure sums in recent years, Ganos noted that it is difficult to predict the final hammer price because uncirculated, high-graded NES cartridges with this specific production history have never appeared on the public market before.Braun and Ganos are offering the majority of the cartridges in the current sale, including three of the five copies awarded the historic perfect 10 grade. Both men are retaining one perfect-grade copy each alongside select high 9-rated copies for their personal collections.
Article Summary: A box of 97 factory-fresh vintage Nintendo video games has officially hit the auction block. The collection consists of 97 uncirculated copies of the classic Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt combination cartridge. These specific copies carry a 1993 manufacturing date – two years after the title was thought to be discontinued. The online sale began through Goldin's Pop Culture Auction and will run through September 9.

Article Title: Tata Play is offering 4 months of Spotify Premium for free: Here's how to claim it
Article Text:
How to claim four months of Spotify Premium through Tata Play

Tata Play Spotify Premium offer : What users get

Tata Play has partnered with Spotify to offer its users four months of Spotify Premium Standard at no additional cost. The offer is available to Tata Play subscribers new to Spotify Premium and includes ad-free music playback, audio quality up to 320kbps, and offline listening. Article Title: Quote of the day by Andrew Carnegie: People who are unable to motivate themselves must be content with mediocrity
Article Text:
What Andrew Carnegie's quote implies

Andrew Carnegie's life and self-motivation

Legendary American industrialist Andrew Carnegie is known for several quotes on self-motivation. Some of them continue to be referenced in discussions on personal and professional growth even today, particularly in contexts involving career development, leadership and goal-setting. One of his quotes reads: "People who are unable to motivate themselves must be content with mediocrity, no matter how impressive their other talents."The statement has been quoted in a variety of contexts, from workplace training materials to motivational writing to public speeches, to distinguish between having ability and actually doing something with that ability. The quote does not specify a profession or context, which makes it applicable in many settings, from business and sports to education and the arts. This means talent alone will not yield results, and self-motivation is another prerequisite.Carnegie’s quote suggests that motivation is an element of its own, distinct from skill and knowledge. This quote implies that someone might have great skills in a certain area, but if they don’t have the motivation to use those skills regularly, those skills might not produce great results. The quote describes self-motivation as something that must come from within and not depend on outside circumstances or acknowledgement.Andrew Carnegie was a Scottish-American industrialist who made his career in the steel industry in the late 19th century. Carnegie was born in Dunfermline, Scotland, in 1835, and immigrated with his family to the United States in 1848, working as a boy in a factory before moving through jobs in telegraphy and railroads. He later founded the Carnegie Steel Company, which was sold in 1901 to become part of US Steel.Often, his rise from factory worker to one of the world’s largest steel operations is mentioned alongside his thoughts on ambition, persistence, and self-driven effort. In the latter part of his life, Carnegie devoted much of his wealth to philanthropy, funding libraries, educational institutions and research organisations throughout the United States and other countries.
Article Summary: Andrew Carnegie was a Scottish-American industrialist who made his career in the steel industry in the late 19th century. One of his quotes reads: "People who are unable to motivate themselves must be content with mediocrity, no matter how impressive their other talents" The statement has been quoted in a variety of contexts, from workplace training materials to motivational writing to public speeches.

Article Title: A high school student won America’s top science award for solving a centuries-old Geometry problem; how his work on 146 rare shapes can change the future of medicine
Article Text:
Image credit: Society for Science

Connor Hill’s geometry research identifies 146 rare shapes

How Connor Hill’s math connects to medicine and science

Why mathematical proofs matter to medical research

Connor Hill’s next step after Regeneron Science Talent Search

“Math is the language that makes scientific ideas usable.”

US high school student Connor Hill won first place at the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search (STS). He has won the award for solving a longstanding problem in geometry involving a class of shapes known as noble polyhedra. His research produced a complete classification of these geometric objects, identifying two infinite families and 146 isolated examples, and earned him the top award from the Society for Science’s competition.The work is rooted in a centuries-old mathematical tradition dating back to Plato and the early study of geometry, but its significance extends beyond the shapes themselves. Hill’s approach involved translating a potentially infinite geometric problem into a finite one using algebra and polynomials. That method of reducing a complex set of possibilities to a manageable number is also used in modern scientific research, including biology, protein structure and drug discovery.Hill’s research focused on noble polyhedra, geometric objects defined by symmetry in which all faces are identical, and all vertices are identical. A cube is a basic example of a highly symmetrical polyhedron, while noble polyhedra relax some of the restrictions found in classical shapes such as the Platonic solids.Hill said his interest in the subject began through an online mathematics community where he encountered the open question surrounding noble polyhedra. What initially appeared to be a search for additional examples eventually developed into a complete proof and classification.A central part of the research was finding a way to reduce the number of possibilities. Rather than attempting to examine an unlimited number of geometric arrangements directly, Hill connected the problem to algebra, including polynomials, which allowed him to convert it into a finite problem that could be solved.The result was the identification of two infinite families of noble polyhedra along with 146 isolated examples.The connection between Hill’s geometry research and medicine lies in the mathematical method rather than in the geometric shapes themselves. Modern biology often involves systems with a large number of possible configurations, making it necessary to identify which possibilities are stable, relevant or biologically meaningful.Henry Wei, MD, Executive Director, Development Innovation at Regeneron, discussed this connection with Hill. Wei is a physician-scientist working at the intersection of biology and medicine.One example is protein structure. Proteins can take on many possible configurations, but only some are stable or relevant to biological processes. Mathematics can help researchers narrow those possibilities and identify structures that may matter for understanding disease or developing medicines.The same principle applies to drug discovery, where researchers need to work through complex biological systems and determine which interactions or structures are most relevant.Hill’s work also demonstrates how a problem can be transformed by moving between different areas of mathematics. His research connected discrete geometry with algebraic geometry to establish a finite framework for a problem that initially involved an effectively unlimited set of possibilities.Modern scientific research frequently uses models and approximations to understand complex systems. Mathematical methods can provide another approach by establishing exact relationships and reducing large sets of possibilities to smaller, more defined problems.Hill said the method used in his project could apply beyond noble polyhedra because the same approach can be useful wherever researchers encounter structure, symmetry or a large number of possibilities that need to be narrowed down.Wei similarly pointed to the role of mathematics in making complex biological systems more understandable. Problems involving protein folding, disease progression, and interactions between treatments and the human body all require researchers to identify patterns within large, complex systems.The connection does not mean Hill’s 146 geometric examples directly produce new medicines. Instead, his research illustrates how mathematical techniques for simplifying complex problems can also be relevant to scientific fields where researchers face similarly large sets of possibilities.Hill is set to attend MIT this fall, with his education supported in part by his winnings from the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search.His research also reflects the role of curiosity-driven mathematics in scientific work. Hill said his project did not begin with a planned breakthrough. It developed gradually as he explored an open mathematical question and connected different areas of mathematics to solve it.The broader relevance of the work lies in that process: reducing a problem that appears infinite to a finite set, establishing an exact solution and then applying the underlying method to other fields where complexity needs to be reduced.As Hill puts it,Science provides concepts, while mathematics formalises them and makes them applicable to specific problems.
Article Summary: US high school student Connor Hill won first place at the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search (STS) He has won the award for solving a longstanding problem in geometry involving a class of shapes known as noble polyhedra. Hill’s approach involved translating a potentially infinite geometric problem into a finite one using algebra and polynomials.

Article Title: USB4 vs USB-C explained: Speeds, cable lengths and the one spec that nobody reads
Article Text:
USB-C is the plug. USB4 is the standard. Knowing which is which decides what you should pay.

The difference between USB4 and USB-C is simple: one is a shape, the other is a set of rules

Is USB-C the same as USB4? Every USB4 cable is USB-C, but almost no USB-C cable is USB4

How to tell if your laptop has USB4, because the port almost never says so

USB4 vs Thunderbolt 4 comes down to certification, not speed, since both stop at 40Gbps

USB4 cable length is the spec nobody reads and the one that quietly ruins setups

USB4 vs USB-C : Which one to buy, and which one do you really need

There is a drawer in most homes now that holds eight or nine cables with the same oval plug on the end, and no way of telling which one is which. One of them charges a laptop. One transfers at speeds that feel like punishment. One came free with a pair of earbuds and does almost nothing beyond keeping them alive. They are physically identical, they all fit every port in the house, and the only difference between them is invisible.That is the whole USB4 versus USB-C problem in one image. USB-C is the shape. USB4 is what the wires inside are allowed to do. The two words turn up on the same spec sheet constantly, often in the same line, which is why they get treated as versions of each other. They are not. A laptop advertising "USB-C ports" has told you nothing about speed, video output or charging. A laptop advertising USB4 has committed to something specific.USB-C arrived in 2014 as a physical redesign. Twenty-four pins, reversible, small enough for a phone and sturdy enough for a workstation. It solved the flipping problem and nothing else. Speed, video and power delivery were all left to whatever protocol the manufacturer decided to run over those pins, which could be anything from USB 2.0 at 480Mbps upward.USB4 is that protocol. The USB Implementers Forum published it in 2019, built on a Thunderbolt 3 specification Intel donated to the group. The number people quote is 40Gbps, but the more useful change is tunnelling. USB4 carries DisplayPort and PCIe traffic alongside ordinary data, and reallocates bandwidth on the fly depending on whether you are copying a file or pushing pixels to a monitor. That is what makes single-cable docking work at all. One connection to a dock and the laptop picks up displays, storage, ethernet and up to 100W of charging, with the Extended Power Range spec reaching 240W on hardware that supports it.Worth sitting with, because it explains most of the confusion. The relationship runs one way. USB4 requires the USB-C connector, so every USB4 cable ends in one. USB-C requires nothing in return, so the majority of USB-C cables in circulation are running much older standards underneath.The chain runs at the speed of its slowest link, and there are three links. Plug a 40Gbps SSD into a USB 3.2 Gen 2 port and you get 10Gbps. Plug that same SSD into a proper USB4 port using a cable that came free in a phone box, and you may get 480Mbps, because the cable is the bottleneck and nothing on screen will tell you so. Files will still copy. They will just take an amount of time that makes no sense given what you paid for the drive.Naming has not helped. USB 3.0 became USB 3.1 Gen 1, then USB 3.2 Gen 1, three names for identical 5Gbps hardware. The USB-IF's response has been to abandon generation numbers in consumer-facing marketing and push speed logos instead, so packaging now reads "USB 40Gbps" or "USB 80Gbps." That is a real improvement, though it only applies to products certified after the change.On the hardware itself, look for a small USB4 marking beside the port, or a Thunderbolt lightning bolt, since Thunderbolt 4 and 5 ports also carry USB4. Plenty of laptops print nothing at all, in which case the spec sheet is the only honest source. Manufacturers also mix port types on the same machine, so the two ports on the left may run at 40Gbps while the one on the right handles 10Gbps and no video. Checking each port individually is tedious and occasionally necessary.The two are close enough that the distinction is mostly about guarantees. Thunderbolt 4 sets a floor: two 4K displays or one 8K, 32Gbps of PCIe bandwidth for storage, mandatory charging support on at least one port. USB4 makes several of those optional, which means one USB4 laptop can drive dual monitors and an external GPU while another handles a single display and refuses the eGPU entirely. Both are correctly labelled.Above that sits USB4 Version 2.0, ratified in 2022 and now on flagship laptops, which doubles throughput to 80Gbps and can run asymmetrically at 120Gbps in one direction for high-refresh displays. Thunderbolt 5 matches it with stricter certification. Whether any of this registers depends entirely on what you connect. For someone editing 4K footage off an external drive, 40Gbps against 10Gbps is the difference between a short wait and a coffee break. For a wired mouse, a keyboard and a printer, it is theoretical.Passive USB4 cables hold full speed only over short runs, roughly 0.8 metres per the specification, which is why certified ones are conspicuously stubby. Longer passive cables drop to half rate. Active cables carry signal-conditioning chips that maintain throughput over greater distances, but they cost more and are less reliably backward compatible with ordinary USB-C peripherals.Power ratings vary independently of all this. A cable can pass 40Gbps and still refuse to charge a laptop, because the wattage it supports is a separate line on a spec sheet most listings never bother to include. In India, a certified 40Gbps cable from a known brand generally runs between Rs 1,500 and Rs 4,000 against a few hundred rupees for an unmarked one. The cheap cable is not fake so much as unspecified, and unspecified is the problem. If a listing states neither a data rate nor a wattage, assume the worst of both.There is no choosing between them, which is the first thing to settle. Buy a USB4 cable and you get USB-C by definition. The actual decision is whether the USB4 premium buys you anything.If you run a dock, an external SSD, an eGPU or a second monitor off your laptop, it does, and the appeal of USB4 is that you stop having to think about any of this. Compliant devices at both ends will negotiate the fastest speeds they support without intervention, and the cable still charges older USB-C hardware because backward compatibility is built in.If all you do is charge a phone and plug in a mouse, it does not. A dedicated 100W power delivery cable running USB 2.0 sells for Rs 400 to Rs 900 and will charge exactly as fast as the Rs 4,000 one, because charging wattage and data throughput are separate specifications that happen to share a plug. Most people need one good USB4 cable for the desk and cheap PD cables everywhere else. Buying the expensive one four times over is the common mistake, and it costs more than the cable that actually needed replacing.Which brings it back to the drawer. It was never lying. It simply never said anything, and neither did most of the people selling the contents. Sort it once, put tape on the fast ones, and the question stops coming up.
Article Summary: The difference between USB4 and USB-C is simple: one is a shape, the other is a set of rules. Knowing which is which decides what you should pay. The relationship runs one way: USB4 requires the USB- C connector, so every USB4 cable ends in one. USB4 carries DisplayPort and PCIe traffic alongside ordinary data.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jensen Huang, ‘The more you buy, the more you save’
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jensen Huang

What Jensen Huang's quote means

Why the line resonates (and gets mocked)

Applying the idea beyond semiconductors

A simple takeaway

Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has spent more than three decades steering it from a scrappy graphics chip maker into the company at the center of the global AI boom, with Nvidia's GPUs now powering everything from video games to the largest AI models in the world. Along the way, Huang has developed a reputation not just for technical vision but for blunt, often counterintuitive one-liners delivered on stage at Nvidia's keynotes. Few have generated as much discussion, and as much good-natured mockery, as this one."The more you buy, the more you save."On its face, the quote sounds like it inverts basic financial logic — spending more money is not usually how anyone ends up saving money. Huang himself has acknowledged the tension directly, once following the line up by calling it "CEO math," adding that it's "not accurate, but it is correct." That qualifier is doing a lot of work. He isn't claiming the arithmetic checks out in a literal sense. He's arguing that from a strategic, systems-level view, larger upfront investment in the right infrastructure can produce disproportionate long-term returns, even if the sticker price climbs.The context matters here. Huang has used the line specifically to describe investment in Nvidia's GPU and networking infrastructure for AI data centers. His argument is that building at scale, investing heavily in accelerated computing rather than trying to get by with smaller, incremental upgrades, ultimately reduces the total cost and energy required to do the same amount of computing work. In other words, the "saving" isn't in the sense of holding onto more cash today. It's in the efficiency gained per unit of computation once the larger system is up and running.Part of what makes the quote memorable is exactly the tension it plays with. It sounds like a walking cliché of corporate spin, the kind of thing said to justify a big expense after the fact. That's precisely why it's been widely shared, sometimes sincerely as an illustration of infrastructure economics, and sometimes as a punchline, including consumer tech outlets jokingly applying the phrase to PC-building shopping sprees that were anything but frugal.But there's a real principle underneath the joke. In large-scale computing, cost efficiency often doesn't scale linearly. A company that invests in a fully built-out, high-performance system can end up paying less per unit of useful output than one that buys smaller, cheaper components piecemeal and stitches them together inefficiently. Huang's framing asks decision-makers to evaluate cost per outcome rather than sticker price in isolation, a shift in thinking that applies well beyond chips and data centers.The logic behind "CEO math" shows up in other investment decisions too, when approached carefully. Buying a higher-quality tool or system upfront, one built to handle a job well rather than just adequately, can reduce the long-run cost of inefficiency, breakdowns, or having to redo work later. The same reasoning applies to hiring, education, or infrastructure of almost any kind: the cheapest option today isn't automatically the cheapest option over time.The caveat, and it's an important one, is that this logic only holds when the larger investment is actually well-targeted. Spending more without a clear efficiency payoff isn't strategic, it's just spending more. Huang's own framing depends entirely on the assumption that the additional expense buys genuine capability and efficiency gains, not simply a bigger price tag.The quote works best as a prompt to look past the initial cost of a decision and ask what it actually buys in terms of long-term value. The next time a larger upfront investment feels wasteful on the surface, the more useful question isn't "is this expensive?" but "does this genuinely reduce cost or increase output per dollar over time?" Huang's line is deliberately provocative precisely because it forces that question into the open, even while admitting, with a wink, that the math doesn't quite add up the way it sounds.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has spent more than three decades steering it from a scrappy graphics chip maker into the center of the global AI boom. Huang has developed a reputation not just for technical vision but for blunt, often counterintuitive one-liners delivered on stage at Nvidia's keynotes.

Article Title: Government issues ‘high-risk’ warning for Google Chrome users: How to protect against hacking
Article Text:
Representative image

How the attack works

How to protect yourself

update Google Chrome on desktop

Open Google Chrome on your PC or Mac.

Click the three-dot menu icon in the top-right corner of the browser window.

Hover over Help in the drop-down menu and select About Google Chrome.

Chrome will automatically check for the latest update and download it.

Click Relaunch to complete the installation and activate the security patches.

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued a high-severity security advisory warning millions of desktop Google Chrome users about multiple critical vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely compromise targeted devices. According to the vulnerability note released by the cybersecurity agency, the security flaws impact Google Chrome across Windows, macOS and Linux systems. These vulnerabilities may create a direct risk of unauthorised remote code execution, system takeover, and denial-of-service (DoS) conditions.The agency explained that the vulnerabilities stem from memory management issues, specifically “use-after-free” errors within core components of the browser, including V8, TabStrip, HTML, Extensions, and Blink.A remote attacker can exploit these flaws by tricking a user into clicking a malicious link or visiting a specially crafted web page. Article Title: US Immigration authority to H1-B visa holders, students and other visa holders: These forms will be rejected starting September 15
Article Text:
USCIS says no grace period will be available for Form I-539 and Form I-765 change

What are Form I-539 and Form I-765

USCIS says no grace period for form change

“If filing Form I-539, please note that USCIS will:

Accept the 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted before Sept. 15, 2026;

Reject the 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026; and

Only accept the 09/15/26 edition of Form I-539 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026.

If filing Form I-765, please note that USCIS will:

Accept the 08/21/25 edition of Form I-765 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted before Sept. 15, 2026;

Reject the 08/21/25 edition of Form I-765 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026; and

Only accept the 09/15/26 edition of Form I-765 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026."

The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has announced that two of its important immigration forms will be replaced with new editions, starting September 15. The change will be applicable to Form I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status, and Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (edition date for both: 09/15/26). The agency further stated that from September 15, it will only accept the 09/15/26 editions of these forms, clarifying that applications with old forms will get rejected. In its official announcement, the immigration authority said that the revised forms “align with the recently published Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media final rule”.“On Sept. 15, 2026, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services will publish revised editions of Form I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status, and Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (edition date for both: 09/15/26),” the agency said adding “The 09/15/26 editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 replace the 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 and the 08/21/25 edition of Form I-765”.Used by H-1B visa holders, students and other visa holders, the I-539 form is for immigration status, while the I-765 form is for work authorization.Form I-539: Used to extend or change a nonimmigrant visa status while in the US. The H-1B worker does not use I-539 to extend or change H-1B status. The employer generally files Form I-129. However, H-1B dependents (H-4 spouses and children) can use I-539 to extend or change their status.Form I-765: Used to apply for work permission, also known as an Employment Authorization Document (EAD). An H-1B worker generally does not use I-765 for their H-1B work authorization. However, certain H-4 spouses may use I-765 to apply for an Employment Authorization Document (EAD), if they meet the eligibility requirements.In the announcement, USCIS further clarifies that there is no grace period for the revised editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 because the revised editions are necessary for USCIS to apply the final rule.“Because there will be no grace period, USCIS is providing preview versions of the 09/15/26 editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 with their instructions. Article Title: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after food safety checks
Article Text:
Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart after food safety checks

Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart licences suspended

Zepto outlet in Pune found with expired food

Blinkit facilities flagged over temperature, hygiene

Zepto and Instamart outlets face food storage violations

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 14 food businesses linked to quick-commerce platforms Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart. The development comes after a statewide inspection drive on August 13 that found several food safety and hygiene violations. According to a report by PTI, the inspection drive covered 86 establishments involved in storing, selling and delivering food through online platforms. The inspections covered food storage, temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, worker hygiene, food safety records and compliance with required food handling practices.As reported by PTI, the FDA also issued 60 improvement notices and directed one facility to temporarily stop operations, the news agency stated.Of the 14 suspended licences, five were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto and two to Instamart. One licence each was suspended for Bhagwati Stores and Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd. The FDA said its inspections focused on whether food businesses were following prescribed safety and hygiene rules while storing and handling products.Officials checked storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest management and personal hygiene of food workers.They also checked food safety records, display of licences and inventory systems such as First In, First Out (FIFO) and First Expired, First Out (FEFO).In Pune, the FDA suspended the licence of a Zepto outlet in Lohegaon after inspectors found food products stored beyond their declared "use by" dates. Officials also found unhygienic storage conditions, inadequate pest control and lapses in the personal hygiene of workers. The FDA said the response given by the company during the hearing was unsatisfactory.Another Pune facility operated by Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd was found to have a cockroach infestation. Inspectors also reported problems with cold-chain maintenance for frozen products and deficiencies in hygiene and pest control.A Blinkit facility in Malad, Mumbai, was found operating with chiller temperatures above the prescribed limit. The FDA also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone mandatory medical examinations, and the required records were not available.Officials further found that some workers were not using protective equipment such as gloves, aprons and head coverings. Damaged storage racks, poor organisation and inadequate separation of different food categories were also reported.At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, inspectors found issues involving drainage, waste disposal, temperature control and housekeeping. The outlet scored 46% during the inspection and was classified as non-compliant.Inspections at Zepto facilities in Mulund and Goregaon found deficiencies related to food storage, temperature management, cleanliness and licence display. At an Instamart outlet in Andheri, inspectors found food packets stored directly on the floor. The FDA also reported inadequate storage space, overcrowding and problems with hygiene and temperature control.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration has suspended licences of 14 food businesses linked to Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart. The development comes after a statewide inspection drive on August 13 that found several food safety and hygiene violations. The inspections covered food storage, temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, worker hygiene and compliance with required food handling practices.

Article Title: Apple threat notifications: What is mercenary spyware and how to protect against it
Article Text:
What exactly is Apple's threat notification

What to do if you get Apple threat notification

General security tips for everyone

Apple recently sent notifications to customers who it suspected to have been targeted with spyware in their devices. The tech giant later confirmed to multiple publications that it sent out the notifications on Thursday to users targeted in 110 countries. By sending these alerts, the company reminded users about one of the most sophisticated digital threats currently in existence: mercenary spyware. If you are one of those who got the term “Apple threat notification” flashing on your screen and wondered what it actually means, here's a breakdown of what these alerts are, why they are sent and what you should do if you ever receive one.Apple threat notifications exist for one specific purpose: to warn and assist users who may have been individually targeted by spyware attacks. In this case, it was a notification for mercenary spyware. These operations are far more advanced than regular cybercrime, and attackers behind them pour in exceptional resources to go after a very small, specific group of people and their devices.Apple says that these attacks cost millions of dollars to carry out and often don’t stay active for very long, which actually makes them harder to detect and stop in time.The good news, though, is that the majority of users will never come across this kind of attack in their lifetime.Citing public reporting and research conducted by civil society groups, cybersecurity researchers, and journalists over the years, Apple says that this level of individually targeted, high-cost cyberattacks has typically been linked to state actors, including private firms that build mercenary spyware for governments, such as the NSO Group's well-known Pegasus tool. While only a small number of individuals end up being targeted, usually journalists, activists, politicians, and diplomats, these attacks are happening constantly and across the globe.If you ever receive one of these alerts, Apple provides extra guidance and recommends steps you can take to secure your accounts and devices, including turning on Lockdown Mode. The company also strongly recommends reaching out to expert organisations for help, such as the Digital Security Helpline run by the nonprofit Access Now, which offers round-the-clock emergency security assistance.While most people will never encounter mercenary spyware, it's still worth following some basic cybersecurity habits.The first is to keep your devices updated with the latest software so you're covered by the newest security patches, and protect them with a passcode, Face ID, or Touch ID.The second most important thing to do is to turn on two-factor authentication along with a strong password for your Apple Account, and enable Stolen Device Protection for extra peace of mind.While Apple doesn’t allow installing apps from third-party stores, ensure that you download apps only from the App Store, use strong and unique passwords across your accounts, opt for passkeys wherever they're availableFinally, Avoid clicking on links or opening attachments sent by unknown senders.
Article Summary: Apple recently sent notifications to customers who it suspected to have been targeted with spyware in their devices. The tech giant confirmed to multiple publications that it sent out the notifications on Thursday to users targeted in 110 countries. By sending these alerts, the company reminded users about one of the most sophisticated digital threats currently in existence: mercenary spyware.

Article Title: In 2024, a Google Maps User was planning a trip using the app; and what he found was a giant meteorite crater that…
Article Text:
Representative Image

Shatter cones and melt rock: how geologists confirmed the Quebec impact crater

Why Uhackatik is one of the biggest meteorite crater discoveries in years

Joël Lapointe was doing something entirely ordinary. The Canadian amateur astronomer had Google Maps open in 2024, scrolling through Quebec's Côte-Nord region to plan hiking routes for a camping trip. Somewhere north of Magpie, around Lake Marsal, the terrain stopped looking like terrain. It looked like a ring—a near-perfect circular scar pressed into the forest, roughly 25km across. His first instinct was to talk himself out of it. Surely someone had already logged this. Lapointe went through the crater databases he knew of and came up empty, so he filed a report with Impact Earth, a crowdsourced crater registry run out of Western University in Ontario. Two years later, that hunch has a name. The structure is now called Uhackatik, and geologists say a meteorite carved it out about 390 million years ago.Planetary geologist Gordon Osinski, who manages Impact Earth, was sceptical at first—most reports he receives turn out to be nothing. He co-led an expedition to the site anyway in October 2025, and the terrain fought back. Osinski, who has done 25 Arctic expeditions across six continents, described it as among the toughest he has attempted, with brutal ground and relentless bugs.Day two settled it. The team found shatter cones, the branching fracture patterns that form when a shockwave rips through rock and point back towards the impact. They also found large exposures of impact melt rock—stone liquefied by the strike, then recooled—which usually erodes away long before anyone gets to see it. Traces of zircon added to the case.Only about 200 impact craters have been confirmed worldwide, and one or two turn up annually, typically in the 5–10km range. Uhackatik is several times that. Osinski reckons the last find of comparable scale was the Hiawatha structure spotted under Greenland's ice in 2018, whose size and origin remain disputed. This one isn't ambiguous.The 390-million-year date puts the impact well before dinosaurs existed—the earliest species appear around 230 million years ago. The name came after consultation with the Innu Council of Ekuanitshit, on whose traditional lands it sits. Findings go to the Meteoritical Society's annual meeting in Frankfurt this month, ahead of peer review.Google Maps and Google Earth have cracked open discoveries beforeSatellite imagery has form here. Egypt's remarkably intact Kamil Crater surfaced through a Google Earth search in 2008. That same year, palaeoanthropologist Lee Berger used it to pinpoint the South African cave system that yielded Australopithecus sediba.As Lapointe put it, ordinary citizens don't find 390-million-year-old craters every day.
Article Summary: A Canadian amateur astronomer found a crater on Google Maps in 2024. The structure is now called Uhackatik, and geologists say a meteorite carved it out about 390 million years ago. The 390-million-year date puts the impact well before dinosaurs existed.

Article Title: Fireflies.ai brings its AI notetaker to the inbox with Email Assistant, now free on all plans
Article Text:
Meeting context is the part rival AI email tools can't copy

Fireflies.ai, the AI meeting assistant used by more than 20 million people and teams at 75% of Fortune 500 companies, has moved into the inbox. On Friday the company launched Email Assistant, which plugs into Gmail or Outlook and treats email the way it already treats calls—sorting what lands, labelling it by priority, and dropping drafted replies into the thread before you get to them.The pitch rests on a familiar arithmetic. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index found the average worker receives 117 emails a day, with 40% of people online at 6am already checking mail and nearly a third back at it by 10pm—the "infinite workday" Microsoft has been warning about. Fireflies' argument is simpler than most: if it sat in on the call, it already knows what the reply should say.That is the actual differentiator here. When a prospect or candidate follows up on something discussed weeks ago, Email Assistant pulls from both the thread and past meetings with that person, so users aren't reconstructing the conversation from memory. Auto Labels triages incoming mail without touching existing rules or filters. Auto Draft Replies writes in a tone set through custom Writing Instructions, and nothing sends without review. If a sent email goes quiet, a follow-up is drafted in the same thread after a waiting period you configure. AskFred handles plain-English requests—find an email, summarise a thread, pull this week's action items.Insights from email now also feed the Daily Brief alongside meetings and Slack. Meeting Prep, Tasks and AI Skills will draw on email context in the coming months.Email Assistant is available today across all plans, including the free tier. Pro starts at Rs 955 per seat per month, billed annually. Fireflies says it does not train its models on customer data.
Article Summary: Fireflies.ai's Email Assistant plugs into Gmail or Outlook and treats email the way it already treats calls. It pulls from both the thread and past meetings with that person, so users aren't reconstructing the conversation from memory. Email Assistant is available today across all plans, including the free tier.

Article Title: Trump’s family crypto venture, World Liberty Financial gets conditional US bank charter approval
Article Text:
USD1 stablecoin could move under World Liberty

OCC sets conditions for the bank

A US banking regulator has conditionally approved a bank charter application linked to President Donald Trump and his family's crypto venture, World Liberty Financial. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) said it granted preliminary approval to World Liberty Trust Company's application for a national trust charter. The company applied for the charter in January this year. If it receives final approval, the trust bank would be able to hold and manage assets for customers and settle payments. The charter would also allow World Liberty to directly issue its USD1 stablecoin and hold the US dollar assets backing it.According to a report by Reuters, the OCC published a letter on August 14 granting conditional preliminary approval to World Liberty Trust Company's application for a national trust charter. However, the approval is not yet final. The company must meet conditions set by the regulator before receiving the charter.The charter could give World Liberty more control over its USD1 stablecoin business. If approved, World Liberty Trust could directly issue USD1 and hold the US dollar assets that support the stablecoin. Those activities are currently handled by business partner BitGo.Welcoming the decision, Zach Witkoff, president and chairman of World Liberty Trust, said: "A national trust bank brings USD1 issuance, custody, and reserve management together under OCC supervision, examined on the same standards that have governed banks for generations.We welcome continuous scrutiny from Federal regulators for many years to come".As mentioned above, the preliminary approval comes with several conditions. World Liberty Trust must notify the OCC about major changes to its business plan, maintain at least $20 million in capital and hire a qualified employee to serve as its internal audit manager.The OCC also addressed concerns about non-US investors in World Liberty Financial.The regulator said those investors were not considered principal shareholders of the proposed bank. It also said several investors had signed "passivity agreements" promising not to control or influence the bank's operations or decisions. One of those signatories was Eric Trump, the president's son, who signed as president of a Trump-family affiliated investment vehicle.
Article Summary: OCC conditionally approves World Liberty Trust Company's application for a national trust charter. If approved, the trust bank would be able to hold and manage assets for customers and settle payments. The charter would also allow World Liberty to directly issue its USD1 stablecoin and hold the US dollar assets backing it.
